track: C (track history -> future path -> uncertainty: the system's prediction OUTPUT, as deployed)
registered: see the git commit that added this file (2026-10-05): before C1's VAL pass, before any corpus-v2 detection cache exists and before C3
class: controlled experiment on corpus-v2 VAL; forecasters are C1's (trained on TRAIN, fixed by sha256) and C1's TRAIN-tuned classical forecasters; nothing is fitted on VAL except the tracker settings, which come from C3's cross-fitting; TEST untouched
question: When the history is what the deployed tracker actually produced from a causal detector (noisy boxes, misses, re-acquisitions), which forecaster predicts the GROUND-TRUTH future path best and with calibrated uncertainty -- and does noise-augmented training help there?

inputs.primary: VAL caches of v2_causal_g4_s0_e20 (zero look-ahead), corpus v2
inputs.histories: ste_cv (experiments/systems/scripts/ste.py) run under the SOT protocol with the cross-fitted settings of C3's report for the same cache (each VAL half uses the other half's settings); a frame enters the history only when the tracker associated a detection there (modes init / track / reacquired; coasted predictions are not measurements)
inputs.targets: ground-truth centres at t+1..t+24 where the target is visible (official annotations)

samples: anchor t: tracker associations at t and t-1, target visible at t in the ground truth, >= 1 visible ground-truth frame in t+1..t+24; history t-15..t (causal by construction: tracker outputs at frames <= t, from a zero-look-ahead detector)

forecasters.classical: each domain's C1 reference (TRAIN-tuned) and the TRAIN-calibrated Kalman (results/runs/aerotrack_temporal/c1/classical_tuning.json)
forecasters.learned_clean: C1 model family, abs inputs, seeds 0 / 1 / 2 (results/runs/aerotrack_temporal/c1, sha256 in learned_registry.json)
forecasters.learned_aug: the same family trained on augmented histories (C1 'aug' arm), seeds 0 / 1 / 2

metrics: as C1 (per domain pooled ADE over h = 1..24, FDE@24, error by horizon, NLL, 50 / 68 / 90 / 95 % coverage, calibration error; cluster bootstrap over sequences, B = 2000)

H1b_point.comparison: learned_clean vs the domain's classical reference, each seed
H1b_point.rule: C1 H1 rule (all seeds: rel <= -5 % and CI upper < 0 -> SUPPORTED; all seeds CI lower > 0 -> LOSES; else NOT_SUPPORTED)

H4_augmentation.comparison: learned_aug vs learned_clean, seed i vs seed i
H4_augmentation.SUPPORTED: all 3 pairs: rel ADE <= -2 % and CI upper < 0

adoption_rule: the system's forecast output per domain = the learned family (aug variant if H4 SUPPORTED, else clean) where H1b is SUPPORTED and H2b is not LOSES; elsewhere the domain's classical reference with its TRAIN-residual variance (C3 prep); C1 (oracle histories) alone never decides deployment

component_gate.measured_failure: forecast_eval (v1, symmetric detector): Kalman forecasts from tracker outputs are no better than zero velocity on Anti-UAV and their 95 % ellipses cover 0.73
component_gate.why: tracker histories add detection noise and gaps to the camera-motion problem C1 isolates
component_gate.baseline: domain classical reference and calibrated Kalman on the same histories
component_gate.novelty: the realistic evaluation of the stack's prediction output (causal detector -> tracker -> forecaster) against ground truth, with calibration
component_gate.cost: as C1 (CPU, microseconds to < 1 ms per forecast)
component_gate.isolating_ablation: same histories for every forecaster; aug vs clean isolates training-time noise
component_gate.falsifier: H1b NOT_SUPPORTED / LOSES everywhere: the deployed prediction output stays classical

run_order: after C3 (its cross-fitted ste_cv settings) on the same caches

amendments.when: 2026-10-05, before any C1c training and before this experiment's first run
amendments.what: the learned forecaster per domain is the one offered by the C1 / C1c adoption rule (preregistration/C1c_domain_aware_forecasting.json): the C1c model where C1c offers it, else C1's pooled model where C1 adopted it, else none
amendments.why: C1's pooled model loses on CST; C1c (registered before its training) tests camera-mode-aware models; downstream experiments must use whichever the registered rules adopt, decided without seeing their own results
